newsitem.title: USA: US Senate tax bill targets corporate spin-offs.
newsitem.headline: US Senate tax bill targets corporate spin-offs.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth's tax legislation would eliminate tax breaks for certain corporate spin-offs unless such stock distributions are conducted only among affiliated businesses.
The provision, which is expected to raise about $1.5 billion over the next five years, does not go as far as a similar measure passed last week by the House Ways and Means Committee.

The Senate version aims to put an end to misuse of "Morris Trusts." Using these trusts, corporations have been allowed to spin-off tax-free to their shareholders units of companies they acquire. Under the bill, only internal transactions would be allowed the favored tax treatment.

The Delaware Republican's tax bill, like the House tax package, would also close another corporate tax loophole by imposing a tax in many cases on investors who sell short stock that they own, a provision expected to raise $708 million.
This technique known as "shorting against the box" allows an investor to effectively sell a stock holding without triggering capital gains.
